blocks.title: Standard enthalpy change of combustion
blocks.text: The standard enthalpy change of combustion, delta Hc, is the enthalpy change when one mole of a substance is completely burnt in excess oxygen under standard conditions. It is always exothermic.

The standard enthalpy of combustion of ethanol is -1368 kJ per mol: C2H5OH(l) + 3O2(g) gives 2CO2(g) + 3H2O(l). The enthalpy change of combustion is useful in calculating the calorie content of foods and fuels.

blocks.prompt: Write the equation that defines the standard enthalpy of combustion of methane, CH4.
blocks.explanation: CH4(g) + 2O2(g) gives CO2(g) + 2H2O(l), for one mole of methane burnt completely in excess oxygen at 298 K and 1 atm; its delta Hc is negative.

items: Delta Hc: one mole burnt completely in excess oxygen under standard conditions, always exothermic (ethanol -1368 kJ per mol); used for the calorie content of foods and fuels.
